arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Sat Nov 21: the first date. Falafel at Avi's, the park ('seventy percent here, thirty is thinking'; 'if someone offered you something... somewhere else' and the 04 number cut in), Doctor Moreau, eleven sorries he counted himself. Under the street lamp she kissed his cheek: 'Not bad. Big. Wednesday, after your Pump House thing, at the café.' Sun: she texts about the dog-faced man; he sends the Moshe photo the same day. Next: midpoint Wed Nov 25, Lior lets it slip before she can.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: 'the system ate November', payment moved to Thursday; Ishai: 'a team pays the team', wants it in writing. Gadi asked about Ruti; Ishai told the truth (she emailed, no answer). Gadi's email: 'Thursday-ish'. The reply to Ruti ('Yes, I take jobs directly') sits in drafts. Next: Thursday comes; week 3 Gadi asks for January.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Sat: went home ('no excuse... no reason'), the box 'like a film'. Sun Nov 22 night: phones for the date report from a flat that echoes ('feng shui'; 'I sound like someone in a big empty room, which I am'; 'I have to get used to it'); Tomer comes Monday for a socket. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19: the toaster refund; 'I want to be paid for what I already did'. Yael let slip Noa paid cash. Homework (a no to someone he likes) used on Noa's plumbers, then on Gadi's Shabbat 'tiny thing'. Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Sat: Eli's last video call March 2022. Sun Nov 22: Ishai brings her the date story with the cats' breakfast and says Toronto is awake; she sends him to the cats. Moti, downstairs: 'nobody is that busy; why doesn't SHE call?' Next: week 3, Ishai quietly messages Eli.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22: Ishai finally asks about the envelope and the proverbs. Avi: 'January is always bad'; he'll tell him after the poker night; one proverb: 'the oil doesn't care what January says'. Next: the telling (Tue/Wed).
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed: chapter thirteen, the coat for a cold city; 'up north'. Fri: chapter fourteen, 'the barista practises the names of streets she has never walked'; asks Ishai if he knows streets up north. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself ('the man in your book sounds like a pushover'). Sun: no café visit.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Sat: phoned Ishai three times about the date ('for science'); Noa dodges his texts. Mon Nov 23: he goes to Noa's to look at a socket (she told Ishai Sunday night). Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat Nov 21: 'listen to what she doesn't say'; 'ask where she is tonight' (Ishai asked it in the park, it worked). Next: Ishai tells him how it went.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: Sun Nov 22 at Avi's: Boaz checks 'eight, fifty, small notes', warns about Ronit; Yossi meets Ishai, the cap 'on holiday since summer', tells him to bring 'a little extra, for emergencies'. Moti: don't sit next to the cap. First night Mon Nov 23 (engine). After it: Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200.
arcs.secret: Yossi is broke: the lucky cap hasn't paid in months, and he owes money at the depot.

beats.goal: Back from the lecture, Ishai keeps yesterday's promise: the cats' breakfast and the story of the date. Mrs. Levi, still coughing, in a thick cardigan and scarf at her door, wants every detail (the horror film, the arm grabbed twice, the cheek kiss, 'Wednesday, something big'). He gently mentions it is Sunday morning in Toronto; she sends him to the cats. Downstairs by the building door, Moti watches him feed the cats and says it plainly for the first time: nobody is that busy; why doesn't SHE call? Then poker tomorrow: small notes, and don't sit next to Yossi's cap.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi wants the whole date story. Moti wants to talk Toronto.
beats.forceText: Ishai tells Mrs. Levi about the date at her door, then feeds her cats downstairs while Moti says Eli isn't really busy.

forceLines.say: Nu? You promised me a story with the cats' breakfast.
She kissed my cheek. And said Wednesday.

forceCommentary.say: Mrs. Levi got the date report before Noa. The building has a chain of command.
Sunday morning in Toronto. Nobody dialled.

moments.text: Ishai comes up the stairs from the lecture with a bag of cat food. Mrs. Levi opens her door in a thick cardigan and a scarf, a tissue up her sleeve, waiting for the story he promised.

lines.say: Nu? You promised me a story with the cats' breakfast.
The cats first. Then the story.
The cats can wait. They're cats. Come in? No, you'll catch it. Stand.
Falafel at Avi's. The park. A horror film.
A horror film. On a first date. Who chose?
Nobody. It was Saturday's film.
And?
She grabbed my arm. Twice. She says once.
Twice. Women always say once.
And at the door...
She kissed my cheek.
Ha! The cheek is a door, motek. Not a house. But a door.
Then she said she'll tell me something. Wednesday. Something big.
Big. Big is never a small word.
That's what I said! Last night. To the radio.
You talk to the radio too? Like me. Terrible.
How's the cough?
Better. Moti brings soup that tastes of Moti.
It's Sunday morning in Toronto, you know. Early. Quiet.
Go feed the cats, Ishai.

commentary.say: 'The cheek is a door, not a house.' Mrs. Levi, write a book.
'Go feed the cats.' The Toronto department is closed today.

update.memory: Ishai brought the date story: horror film, arm grabbed twice, a cheek kiss, 'something big' Wednesday. He said Toronto is awake. I sent him to the cats.

moments.text: By the building door Ishai shakes dry food into the cats' dish; Ben-Gurion pushes the others aside. Moti comes out with the committee folder under his arm and stops to watch.

lines.say: Ben-Gurion is getting fat on your watch.
He eats for three. The others let him.
Like the committee. How was the barista?
Does the whole building know?
Mrs. Levi knows. So, yes.
It was good. Really good.
Good. Now. She showed you the phone yesterday.
March 2022. She keeps a heart next to his name.
And she told you he's busy.
Toronto is busy. Every time.
Nineteen years across the hall from her. Nobody is that busy.
So why doesn't he call?
That's his business. Why doesn't SHE call?
Because then it's her fault if he doesn't answer.
Look at that. The quiet one thinks.
Should I say something to her?
To her? No. Tomorrow night, poker. Bring small notes.
Boaz said fifty. Small notes.
And don't sit next to Yossi's cap. It has opinions.

commentary.say: Nineteen years across the hall. Moti files feelings under committee business.
'Why doesn't SHE call?' Moti just did the whole season in one line.

update.memory: Fed the cats with Ishai. Told him about Eli: nobody is that busy. He understood why she won't call. Poker tomorrow, small notes.

beats.goal: Sunday: the day Gadi promised the payment date. Gadi phones all cheer: the 'system migration' ate November, now it's Thursday. Ishai holds firm (no small things before the number; 'a team pays the team') and asks for the date in writing today. Gadi asks, too casually, whether Ruti contacted him directly; Ishai says honestly she emailed and he didn't answer. The email that comes says 'Thursday-ish'. Ishai opens his draft to Ruti, types 'Yes, I take jobs directly', and leaves it unsent. Then Dana texts about the film, and he sends her a Moshe photo at once.
beats.teaser: Gadi promised a payment date for Sunday. It's Sunday.
beats.forceText: Gadi phones: the payment moves to Thursday because of 'the system'. Ishai asks for it in writing and leaves a reply to Ruti in drafts.

forceLines.say: So. Ofer migrated the system. It ate November.
A team pays the team, Gadi.

forceCommentary.say: 'The system ate November.' Somewhere an accountant felt a chill.
No sorry! Did everyone hear the no sorry?

moments.text: Ishai at his desk, the Sababa invoice from November 8 open on the screen. His phone rings: Gadi. He takes a breath and answers.

lines.say: Ishai! Sunday! Did you rest? You sound rested.
It's Sunday, Gadi. You said Sunday. The number.
The number, yes. Big day for numbers.
Five thousand five hundred. When?
So. Ofer migrated the system. It ate November.
It ate November.
Temporarily! Thursday it spits it out. Promise.
You promised Sunday. On Friday. At night.
And I meant it on Friday. Meanwhile, a tiny thing—
No tiny things. Not before the number.
Okay, okay. Look at you. Is this the class?
Yes, actually.
Tell me. Did Ruti call you? Directly?
She emailed. Thursday. I didn't answer.
Good. Good. Send her to me. We're a team.
A team pays the team, Gadi.
Ha! Thursday. In writing, if you want. I'll email.
Email it today. With a date on it.
Today. Thursday. With a date. Ciao, genius!

commentary.say: 'The system ate November.' Somewhere an accountant felt a chill.
'A team pays the team.' Ishai! Who are you and where's the sorry?

update.memory: Ishai wanted the number on Sunday. Told him the system ate November, Thursday. He admitted Ruti emailed him. Wants the date in writing today.

moments.text: Twenty minutes later an email from Gadi lands. Ishai reads it twice, then opens his draft to Ruti from Thursday, types one line, and leaves the cursor blinking over SEND.

message.say: As promised, in writing: payment Thursday-ish, after the migration. Love the dreidel! Tiny change on it tomorrow. G.

lines.say: Thursday-ish. That's not a date. That's a weather forecast.
'Yes, I take jobs directly.' ...Not yet. Drafts.

commentary.say: His finger is RIGHT there. Send it! No, don't. No, send it!
Saved to drafts. The most dangerous folder in Tel Aviv.

moments.text: His phone buzzes again: Dana. He laughs out loud, walks straight to the counter and photographs Moshe and the sprout from three angles.

message.say: Popcorn hangover. The man with the dog face was in my dream. Your fault. Is Moshe still alive?

lines.say: A photo. Right now. Not in a week.
Moshe, chin up. Leaves up. She's looking.

commentary.say: Same-day Moshe photo. Character development, live on air.
Three angles of a basil. Moshe's agent will want a cut.

beats.goal: The evening before poker, at Avi's kiosk. Boaz, just off his bus shift, checks Ishai remembers (eight, fifty, small notes) and warns him about Ronit and that Yossi's cap has been 'on holiday' since summer. Yossi arrives from the depot in overalls and the lucky cap, sizes Ishai up, laughs too loud and tells him to carry 'a little extra cash, for emergencies'. Then Ishai, alone at the counter, finally asks Avi about the envelope and the missing proverbs; Avi says he'll tell him after the card game, and gives one proverb about January.
beats.teaser: Ishai meets Yossi and the famous lucky cap at Avi's.
beats.forceText: At Avi's kiosk Boaz introduces Ishai to Yossi before poker; Avi promises to explain his envelope after the game.

forceLines.say: A man should carry a little extra. For emergencies.

forceCommentary.say: 'A little extra for emergencies.' Yossi, sweetie, whose emergency?
The cap is on holiday. The cap is not the only one.

moments.text: Early evening on Herzl Street, the kiosk's light on, a short queue forming. Boaz, still in his bus driver's jacket, just off shift, waves Ishai over to the counter.

lines.say: The quiet one! Tomorrow, eight o'clock. You remember?
Eight. Fifty shekels. Small notes.
Good. He learns. Ronit will hate you.
Why would she hate me?
She hates people who listen. Talkers are easier to read.
So I should talk more?
You should eat. Avi, two. One with everything.
Moti says don't sit next to Yossi's cap.
Moti counts pizza slices like votes.
Is Yossi good?
Yossi is lucky. Was lucky. Lately the cap is on holiday.
Lately?
Since summer. Don't mention it. He's coming from the depot.
Here? Why?
To see the new one before the cards do. There he is.

commentary.say: 'She hates people who listen.' Ishai has been listening for thirty-one years.
The cap is on holiday since summer. Write that down, people.

update.memory: Met Ishai at Avi's the evening before poker. He remembered: eight, fifty, small notes. Warned him about Ronit, and about Yossi's cap.

moments.text: Yossi arrives in grease-marked overalls and a faded lucky cap, shakes Ishai's hand a beat too long and looks him over like an engine.

lines.say: So this is the quiet one. Hands of a designer.
Hi. Yossi? I've heard about the cap.
Everybody's heard. Nobody touches it.
I won't touch it. Sorry. I wasn't going to.
He apologises to the cap! Boaz, I like him.
Is it really lucky?
Twenty years. Lately it's thinking things over.
Like a phase.
Like a phase. Tell me, tomorrow you bring cash, or apps?
Cash. Fifty. Boaz said.
Only fifty? A man should carry a little extra. For emergencies.
What emergency happens at poker?
Pizza. Rebuys. Life. Ha!
Okay. A little extra, then.
Good man. Avi, put his falafel on my— no. On his. Ha!
On mine. It's fine.

commentary.say: 'A little extra for emergencies.' Yossi, sweetie, whose emergency?
He almost put the falafel on his own tab. Then remembered.

update.memory: Met Ishai at Avi's. The quiet one apologised to my cap. Told him to bring a little extra cash tomorrow. For emergencies.

moments.text: Boaz and Yossi head off toward the depot. Ishai eats at the counter. Avi fries in silence; a small calculator sits by the tahini with the lawyer's envelope tucked under it.

lines.say: You're eating slow tonight. Something wrong with my falafel?
Your falafel is perfect. You're quiet.
I'm frying. Frying is quiet.
You used to give me a proverb. Every pita.
The proverbs are on holiday. With Yossi's luck.
Avi. What's the envelope?
Paper. Paper with a lawyer's name on it.
Is it bad?
It's January. January is always bad.
If you need emails written, I'm good at emails.
You're good at apologising. Emails, we'll see.
I'm serious.
I know. That's why I'm not telling you tonight.
When, then?
After your card game. A man shouldn't play with two worries.
Okay. After.
Eat. And one proverb, because you asked: the oil doesn't care what January says.

commentary.say: A proverb! Small, sad, but a proverb. The kiosk has a pulse.
He ASKED. Out loud. Avi, after poker you're telling him everything.

update.memory: Ishai asked about the envelope and my missing proverbs. I said after his card game. Gave him one, about January.

beats.goal: Late evening, Noa phones for the full date report (he forgot to text after). She cheers the eleven sorries and the cheek kiss, but her voice echoes: she says she is 'rearranging, feng shui'. She asks for popcorn details 'because I need popcorn tonight', mentions Tomer is coming tomorrow to look at a socket ('landlords take a week, Tomer takes a pizza'), says she sounds like someone in a big empty room, 'which I am', turns down the armchair: 'I have to get used to it.' Used to what? 'The feng shui.' Ishai keeps his no-questions promise, barely.
beats.teaser: Noa calls for the date report. Why does her flat echo?
beats.forceText: Noa phones for the date report; her flat echoes and she says she has to 'get used to it'.

forceLines.say: Rearranging. Feng shui. Go on, the cheek.

forceCommentary.say: Feng shui. Sure. And the echo is the chi.
'I need popcorn tonight.' That wasn't about popcorn.

moments.text: Late evening. Ishai in the armchair, Falafel's head on his foot, the radio low. Noa calls. Her voice comes back with a strange hollow echo.

lines.say: Report. Every detail. You promised after, and after was yesterday.
You said text after. I fell asleep.
Unforgivable. Start with the sorries.
Eleven. I counted myself.
Eleven! Ishush, that's a personal best.
And she kissed my cheek.
SHE kissed YOU? Wait, wait. I have to sit down.
Sit on what? Why do you echo?
I'm... rearranging. The living room. Feng shui.
It sounds like a parking garage.
Minimalism. Very trendy. Go on. The cheek.
Under the lamp. Then 'Wednesday. Something big.'
Big like good?
She said not bad. Big.
Then you wait. No detective work.
You're one to talk. 'A film about a box.'
That was a film.
Noa.
Tell me about the popcorn. Please. I need popcorn tonight.

commentary.say: Feng shui. Sure. And the echo is the chi.
'I need popcorn tonight.' That wasn't about popcorn.

moments.text: The call goes on. On Noa's end a door closes with a hollow bang, and she starts talking faster.

lines.say: Anyway! Tomer's coming tomorrow. To look at a socket.
Tomer? Why not your landlord?
Landlords take a week. Tomer takes a pizza.
He called me twice about you. 'Noa sounds weird.'
Tomer thinks a toaster sounds weird.
Do you? Sound weird?
I sound like someone in a big empty room.
Which I am.
Come here. The armchair misses you.
No. I have to get used to it.
Used to what?
The... feng shui. Goodnight, Ishush. Win tomorrow.
I'll lose fifty shekels politely.
Don't be polite. Be lucky. Love you, idiot.
Love you. Call if the sockets need me.
...Ha. Yeah.

commentary.say: 'I have to get used to it.' Ishai. ISHAI. Ask the next question!
He asked 'used to what'. She said feng shui. Furniture one, truth zero.

update.memory: Phoned Ishai for the date report: eleven sorries, a cheek kiss. Called my empty flat feng shui. Tomer comes tomorrow. Said no to the armchair.

hook.text: Noa's flat echoes, she calls it feng shui and says she has to 'get used to it'. Tomer comes Monday for a socket. Get used to what?

previously.text: Nobody got there first. Under the street lamp Dana kissed his cheek: 'Not bad. Big. Wednesday.' Ishai counted his own sorries: eleven.

hosts: Sunday. The day Gadi promised. Place your bets.
Morning after a first date. Ishai slept nine hours. Dana, we assume, less.
Eleven sorries. Counted by the man himself. That's accountability.
A cheek kiss under a street lamp. Herzl Street will never recover.
Today's lecture: Gregor MacGregor, Part 2. A man who sold a country that didn't exist.
Fake country, real money. Gadi, are you taking notes?
Mrs. Levi was promised the date story with the cats' breakfast. She's been waiting since dawn.
Ben-Gurion the cat has gained weight under Ishai's care. Nobody is surprised.
Sunday in Tel Aviv is a Monday wearing a nicer shirt.
Gadi's 'Sunday, promise' was said on Friday night. Friday-night promises have a short shelf life.
Ruti's email has been in his inbox since Thursday. So has his reply. In drafts.
Tomorrow: poker at Boaz's. Fifty shekels, small notes, one lucky cap.
Nobody touches Yossi's cap. That's not superstition. That's building law.
Avi's calculator gets more attention than his fryer lately.
Grey skies, sixteen degrees. Jacket weather. Mrs. Levi approves.
Wednesday is three days away. Ishai has already checked twice.
Moshe has a roommate, a sprout, and now a modelling career.
Falafel slept through the whole date story. He's heard it.
Oren's prediction for today: one email, zero money.
Zohar's prediction for today: one Moshe photo, sent the same day. Growth.
Noa promised to call for the report. Noa promises a lot of things lately.
A horror film on a first date and nobody screamed. Only one arm got grabbed. Twice.
The PixelPlex sold two large popcorns last night. Both to the same row.
Somewhere a man with a dog's face is still haunting Dana's dreams. Ishai's fault, apparently.
Avi's queue at half past six is the city's most honest clock.
Mrs. Levi's game show at seven thirty. Mrs. Levi shouts the answers. Mrs. Levi is usually right.
Today he says no to small things. Let's see if small things hear it.
Thursday improv lesson four is the last one Noa paid for. Big week.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Sunday morning, the week starts whether you like it or not.
Grey and sixteen over Tel Aviv. Bring a jacket, leave the umbrella guessing.
To everyone who had a first date last night: we hope you counted something.
Traffic on the coastal road. Traffic everywhere. Traffic is a state of mind.
This one goes out to everyone waiting on an invoice. Hang in there.
Next, a slow one for people who talk to their plants. You know who you are.
Caller from Herzl Street says her cats are getting fat. Lady, that's love.
Market prices: tomatoes down, lemons up, patience unchanged.
Sunday afternoon, the hour of laundry and good intentions.
Evening on 88.2. If you're eating falafel standing up, you're doing it right.
A song about January, because January always comes. Sorry.
Late on Radio Herzl. Phones down, kettles on, goodnight to the night shift.

zelig: Sunday pigeons are lazier. They know the week is long.
A kiss on the cheek is a question in a polite font.
Bread for the birds, bread for the man. Same bread.
michal: Sunday. Everyone's back pretending they ran on Friday.
Mirror says forty more seconds. Mirror is a liar.
The run club meets Friday. Somebody should go.
sivan: Treadmill nine, again. It knows me now.
Interval three. Breathe. Don't look at the clock.
Some people call ten minutes a warm-up. Some people.
lior: Chapter fifteen. The barista buys a train timetable.
No. 'Timetable' is too cold. Schedule? Departures.
He'd never notice. He notices kerning, not himself.
A man who apologises to his coffee. That line stays.
kobi: Sunday system: numbers that end in two. Two is lucky on Sundays.
Second beer. The system is warming up.
Lottery's Tuesday. The system never sleeps.
Third beer. I can feel the jackpot. In my knees.

street: ...he says the bus is late, I say the bus is a philosophy...
...a whole falafel for twenty? In this economy?...
...my cousin's barista moved to Haifa, can you imagine...
...tell your mother I called, I'm not calling again...
market: ...the lemons are from yesterday, I can smell yesterday...
...two kilos, and don't put the soft ones underneath...
...if you want sweet, buy the small ones...
park: ...he jogs the same loop backwards, says it's better for the knees...
...the duck has a name, I swear, the kids call him Moshe...
...leave the pigeons, they belong to the old man...
...I'm not crying, it's the wind off the sea...
cafe: ...oat milk is a lifestyle, not a milk...
...I'm writing a novel too, well, thinking about it...
...she said she'll answer by December, who answers by December?...
...the new cups are thinner, you can feel it...

chat.say: Good morning. Stair light on the first floor fixed again. Please do not hang on the railing.
Whoever parks the bicycle by the mailboxes: it's a lovely bicycle. Move it.
The cats ate. Ishai is a good boy. The story is private.
Is anyone else's water warm only in the morning?
Reminder: building fees by Thursday. Cash to Moti, receipts given, smiles optional.
Monday 20:00 there will be some noise in apt 2. Cards, not a party. Sorry in advance.
Game show. The man answered Lisbon. It was Madrid. I said Madrid.
Found: one blue glove on the stairs. It's on the mailbox. Lonely.
